claims.claim: The hospitality industry is commonly organized into major sectors: lodging/accommodation; food and beverage; travel and transportation; recreation, attractions and entertainment; and meetings, incentives, conventions and events (MICE).

Hotels are classified both by service level (economy/budget, midscale, upscale, and luxury) and by property type, including full-service, limited-service/select-service, extended-stay, resort, convention, and bed-and-breakfast.

Full-service hotels offer a wide range of on-site amenities including sit-down restaurants and other services, while limited-service (select-service) hotels offer a focused set of amenities and typically operate without a full-service restaurant.

A franchise is a licensing arrangement in which a franchisor licenses its trademarks and business methods to a franchisee, who owns and operates the property and pays fees and royalties in exchange for the brand, central reservations, marketing, and training.

Under a management contract, a management company operates a hotel on behalf of the owner for a fee (often a base fee plus an incentive fee); management can be combined with a brand affiliation or performed for an independent property.

The hospitality industry frequently separates the property owner (who holds the real estate and its capital risk), the operator/manager (who runs the hotel), and the brand/franchisor (who licenses the name, standards, reservation system, and loyalty program) into as many as three distinct parties.

Major hotel companies pursue an asset-light model, expanding mainly through franchising and management rather than owning real estate; IHG reports that about 73 percent of the rooms in its system are franchised, about 27 percent are managed, and under 1 percent are owned or leased.

A REIT (real estate investment trust) is a company that owns and typically operates income-producing real estate such as hotels, and to keep its tax status must distribute at least 90 percent of its taxable income to shareholders as dividends.

Lodging managers earned a median annual wage of $68,130 in May 2024, held about 52,000 jobs in 2024, and their employment is projected to grow 3 percent from 2024 to 2034, with about 5,400 openings projected each year on average.
An independent hotel operates without chain or brand affiliation and is financed and managed by its owners or by a third-party operator, in contrast to a chain-affiliated property.

A hotel franchisee typically pays fees to the franchisor; IHG reports typical franchise royalty fees of about 5-6 percent of rooms revenue and typical management base fees of about 1-3 percent of a hotel's total revenue.

conflictingEvidence.issue: The exact number of hospitality sectors varies by source (four, five, or more).
positions: Some texts group the industry into four sectors (lodging, food and beverage, recreation, travel and tourism).
Others add meetings and events (MICE) as a distinct fifth sector, or split travel and transportation out separately.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Presented the sector list as a common organizing framework rather than a fixed count, and noted that boundaries overlap and taxonomies differ by source.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether a REIT distributes 90 percent or nearly 100 percent of taxable income.
positions: The legal minimum to maintain REIT tax status is distribution of at least 90 percent of taxable income (IRC section 857).
In practice most REITs distribute close to 100 percent to avoid corporate income tax.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Stated the 90 percent legal minimum as the defining requirement and noted that most REITs distribute nearly all taxable income in practice.
